survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD TALIS 2024 Croatia note reports results based on self-reported survey responses collected in 2024 from lower secondary teachers and principals. The note does not describe the analytic subsample construction (e.g., exclusions for non-response, missing items, or specific questionnaire modules) nor does it report any student/teacher sampling weight variable names or replicate-weight procedures. Because TALIS is a complex survey of teachers/principals, the underlying TALIS database typically uses sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates; however, this note does not specify whether weights were applied in the reported tables/figures. The document also does not report any plausible-value or scaling procedures because it presents descriptive percentages and statistically significant differences/changes rather than model-based achievement scores.

It does not specify additional inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., response-rate thresholds, item non-response rules, or whether only specific TALIS modules were used for each figure), so the analytic sample is not further describable from the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS 2024 Croatia note summarizes self-reported information from lower secondary teachers and principals collected in 2024. It reports descriptive distributions (e.g., teachers’ age and gender composition, experience profiles, and shares of teachers working in schools with higher proportions of non-native speakers or refugees) and reports statistically significant differences or changes relative to the OECD average and between 2018 and 2024. The note covers domains including teaching for today’s world (diversity and inclusion), special education needs, social and emotional skills, technology use (including reported AI use), teachers’ learning opportunities (initial teacher education, induction/mentoring, continuous professional learning), teacher leadership and autonomy, professional relationships, status of the teaching profession, employment terms, demands of teaching, and professional outcomes/well-being. No machine-learning models are trained; therefore, there are no predictive metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/RMSE) to interpret. The note also cautions that cross-country comparisons should be interpreted carefully because TALIS relies on self-reports and may be shaped by social and cultural context.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a results note summarizing TALIS 2024 Croatia descriptive statistics and statistically significant comparisons, not an empirical machine-learning study. Consequently, there is no reported ML algorithm, no predictive target variable, and no model performance metrics. The note also does not provide sample sizes or per-country counts in the provided text, so total_students and n_students cannot be extracted from the manuscript body.
